literal: With the good happened than poverty is indeed more painful, with the unlearned happened wealth.
translation: Wealth possessed by the unlearned is far more grievous than poverty suffered by the good.
modern: நல்லவர்களிடம் உள்ள வறுமையை விட, படிக்காதவர்களிடம் உள்ள செல்வம் மிகவும் துன்பம் தருவதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts two situations: poverty among the good and wealth among the unlearned. The comparative suffix 'இன்' (in) attached to 'வறுமை' (poverty) sets up the comparison, meaning 'than poverty'. The word 'இன்னாதே' (is indeed painful/grievous) emphasizes that it is worse for an uneducated person to have wealth than for a good, educated person to suffer poverty, as the unlearned are likely to misuse their wealth and cause harm.
